claims.statement: langgraph.json wires the LangGraph auth object and a custom Starlette app, sets middleware_order to auth_first, enables custom-route authentication, and disables MCP and A2A mounting.
The custom Starlette app (healthcare_rag/agent/http_app.py) installs MemberPerimeterMiddleware, which validates the member-facing HTTP contract before dispatch and applies response checks afterward.

supabase_bearer() verifies a Bearer member request against the configured Supabase user endpoint, sets identity to the returned user id and role to member, copies a bounded control-character-free display name only from the service-writable app_metadata (never user_metadata), and raises 401 on missing configuration, malformed identity, HTTP failure, or invalid JSON.

Internal-service authentication requires both the platform key (x-api-key against LANGSMITH_API_KEY) and the internal token (x-internal-token against COACH_INTERNAL_TOKEN) to match via constant-time comparison; the request's method/path derive a reservation or cron_ops sub-role; reservation traffic supplying x-internal-owner is rejected with 403, and cron_ops principals carry the internal owner only when the header is present.
An OPTIONS request receives an authenticated CORS-preflight principal (role preflight) so the CORS middleware can answer without member credentials.

Authorization handlers scope member data access independently of request-shape validation: thread creation overwrites metadata with the authenticated user_id; thread read, search, and delete are scoped to that user_id; members cannot submit a cron_wake run input; run cancellation is scoped to the owning member; internal reservation access is limited to upload-reservation threads; and an internal cron-wake run is admitted only in its exact shape with matching thread and user scope.

Assistant read/search authorization returns an empty scope filter because assistant records carry no member-identifying metadata; the member request-shape perimeter compensates by restricting assistant search bodies to graph_id == "coach", preventing a member from selecting a different graph despite the metadata-only platform filter.

Cron create/read/search/update/delete authorization is scoped to the internal_owner carried by a cron_ops sub-role principal; create additionally requires the cron payload's metadata.user_id to equal that owner.

Every authorization handler treats a StudioUser context as an unconditional allow (_is_studio short-circuits to None); this principal is only ever issued while langgraph.json leaves disable_studio_auth false.

validate_member_request() rejects non-canonical paths (percent-encoding, double slashes, trailing slash) and denies any method/path/query/body combination outside a small enumerated allowlist, returning a 403 'Route is not available' by default.

Thread creation accepts only an empty object or a body of exactly {metadata: {}, thread_id: <uuid>}; the middleware then rewrites the request body to authenticated ownership metadata (and the supplied UUID thread_id, if valid) before the native handler receives it.

Thread search bodies are restricted to select/limit/offset/sort_by/sort_order, select must be a non-empty subset of a fixed public field projection, limit must be an integer 1-100, offset a non-negative integer, and sort_by/sort_order must be from fixed enumerations.

The direct member run envelope fixes assistant_id to coach, stream_subgraphs to false, durability to exit, and if_not_exists to reject, requires exactly one of input or command, and additionally fixes stream_mode/stream_resumable/multitask_strategy per the HC_RAG_MEMBER_STREAM_PERIMETER version.

Member run input is restricted to question (required unless resuming) and, only alongside the exact document-review question text, an attachment_id; v2 additionally requires attachment_id to be a UUID.
A resume command must be exactly {resume: {accept: bool, fields?: [{key: str, value: str}, ...]}}; no other shape is accepted.

HC_RAG_MEMBER_STREAM_PERIMETER is read once from the environment at import time and defaults to v1; v1 keeps the direct run stream updates-only, non-resumable, and single-task (reject), while v2 requires stream_mode to include updates (optionally plus messages/values), turns on resumability, and enqueues concurrent turns, and v2 additionally admits owned history, run join/join-stream reads, and a constrained cancel query that v1 rejects.

The browser build must set NEXT_PUBLIC_HC_RAG_MEMBER_STREAM_PERIMETER to match the server's HC_RAG_MEMBER_STREAM_PERIMETER because the accepted wire contract differs between versions; production deployment configuration selects v2.

V2 adds ThreadStream transport: POST /threads/{id}/stream/events validates a channel/namespace/depth/since subscription, and POST /threads/{id}/commands accepts only run.start, input.respond, state.get, state.listCheckpoints, and state.fork with per-method parameter validation; checkpoint configuration cannot bind a different thread, interrupt responses are restricted to the root namespace, and unknown methods or mutation-oriented fields fail with 400. V1 rejects both routes outright.
The v2 run-cancel query string is limited to wait/action/timeout with enumerated values and no duplicate keys, and fails with 400 on malformed query encoding or unrecognized keys/values.

The perimeter recognizes a measured CopilotKit/AG-UI run shape on the same /runs/stream route, distinguished from the direct member envelope by payload shape (a command field, or an input carrying copilotkit/ag-ui keys), and validates it against its own narrower, adapter-specific allowlist of fields, stream modes, assistant identifiers, and a resume echo tolerance, rather than the general member run contract.

Copy admission first loopbacks to confirm the caller owns the source thread before allowing a copy, and after the native copy response, verifies that the copied thread's metadata.user_id matches the caller, returning 502 if the response is unreadable or ownership does not match.

Thread deletion first confirms via a loopback self-call that the caller still owns the thread and invokes reminder/cron cleanup preparation, returning a retryable 503 if cleanup is not ready; after the native delete call, it re-checks that the thread no longer exists before clearing the cleanup marker and returning 204.

An attachment referenced by a stream run must match a completed ('done'), unexpired, caller-owned upload-registry record bound to the URL thread and not already admitted; the middleware marks it admitted before graph execution to prevent a second admission, and rejects the run otherwise.

A successful GET /threads/{id}/state response is reduced to values, interrupts, tasks, and next; pending_document_op_id is stripped recursively from values; if any private state channel (question, attachment_id, cron_wake, or pending_document_op_id) has a non-null value anywhere in the projected payload, or the underlying response cannot be parsed/buffered, the entire response is replaced with a 500 'Unsafe state response'.

Custom routes (/coach/uploads, /coach/uploads/{id}/status, /coach/feedback, /coach/internal/version) sit inside the authenticated perimeter; upload-status reads the caller's own registry namespace, feedback confirms the caller can read the nominated thread/state before storing feedback in the caller's namespace, and /coach/internal/version is restricted to the internal role.
The custom app's CORS policy permits only COACH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, credentials, GET/POST/DELETE/OPTIONS methods, and Authorization/Content-Type headers.

The identical healthcare_rag/agent/auth.py Auth instance is enforced by two independent runtimes: the LangGraph platform deployment applies it via langgraph.json's auth.path and the platform's own SDK middleware, while the clean-room agent server (server/auth.py) independently loads the same instance with load_auth_instance and runs it through its own AuthMiddleware/AuthPolicyEngine.

server/auth.py's AuthPolicyEngine.run_policy invokes the same @auth.authenticate/@auth.on handlers as the platform deployment and translates a handler result of None or True into an allow, False into a 403 Forbidden, and a dict into a scope filter.

In the clean-room server, require_scope_match() compares a specific resource's metadata against an authorization scope filter (supporting $eq and $contains term operators) and raises 404, not 403, on a mismatch, so a member cannot distinguish another member's resource from a nonexistent one; merge_scope_filter() instead folds the scope filter into search/list queries so mismatched items are simply omitted from results rather than erroring.
The clean-room server's AuthMiddleware treats /ok and /info as public paths that bypass authentication entirely, matching the native perimeter's exemption of /ok from principal checks.

SERVER_LOCAL_DEV, read only by the clean-room server's AuthMiddleware and off by default, remaps any 401 raised by the authenticate handler (missing credentials, unrecognized keys, or malformed authorization) into a StudioUser('langgraph-studio-user') principal with full authorization-handler access; production deployment deliberately leaves it unset/0 so a 401 on the deployed server always stays a 401.

The perimeter's fail-closed status catalogue is: 401 for missing or failed authentication; 403 by default for invalid member routes/envelopes/ownership under the native member perimeter; 400 for malformed JSON and designated stream-protocol validation errors (checkpoint config, stream/events subscriptions, commands, cancel query); 404 for a clean-room server scope mismatch on a specific resource; 500 for unsafe state projection; 503 for a not-yet-ready delete cleanup; and 502 for a corrupted or ownership-mismatched copy response.
